title: 4.5.4: Chapter Review
originalText:
Hindu-Arabic Positional System

Exercise \(\PageIndex{1}\)

What is the base of \(5^7\) ?

Exercise \(\PageIndex{2}\)

What is the exponent of \(5^7\) ?

Exercise \(\PageIndex{3}\)

Compute \(4^5+3^2\).

Exercise \(\PageIndex{4}\)

Convert the Hindu-Arabic number into expanded form: 4,201.

Exercise \(\PageIndex{5}\)

Convert the expression to a Hindu-Arabic numeral: \(6 \times 10^3+3 \times 10^2+7 \times 10^1+5 \times 10^0\).

Early Numeration Systems

Exercise \(\PageIndex{6}\)

Which systems—Hindu-Arabic, Roman, Mayan, or Babylonian—are additive systems?

Exercise \(\PageIndex{7}\)

Which systems—Hindu-Arabic, Roman, Mayan, or Babylonian—are positional systems?

Exercise \(\PageIndex{8}\)

Which systems—Hindu-Arabic, Roman, Mayan, or Babylonian—use a 0?

Exercise \(\PageIndex{9}\)

In the Babylonian system, what are the place values based on?

Exercise \(\PageIndex{10}\)

In the Mayan system, what are the place values based on?

Convert the Babylonian numeral to a Hindu-Arabic numeral.

[Figure: Babylonian numeral 21 is displayed.]

Exercise \(\PageIndex{12}\)

[Figure: Mayan numeral 8 is displayed.]

Converting with Base Systems

Exercise \(\PageIndex{15}\)

List the numbers from 0 to 100 in base 5.

Exercise \(\PageIndex{16}\)

In base 8, what is the place value of the 3 in the number 638_(8)?

Exercise \(\PageIndex{17}\)

How many symbols are needed for a base 17 system?

Exercise \(\PageIndex{18}\)

What does it mean for a number to be in base 6?

Exercise \(\PageIndex{19}\)

What symbols are used in a base 12 system?

Exercise \(\PageIndex{20}\)

When converting from a base 10 number to a base 2 number, would the number of digits decrease?

Exercise \(\PageIndex{21}\)

Convert 311_(5) to base 10.

Exercise \(\PageIndex{22}\)

Convert 45_(12) to base 10.

Exercise \(\PageIndex{23}\)

Convert 1001_(2) to base 10.

Exercise \(\PageIndex{24}\)

Convert 459 to base 8.

Exercise \(\PageIndex{25}\)

Convert 1198 to base 12.

Exercise \(\PageIndex{26}\)

Convert 38 to base 2.

Exercise \(\PageIndex{27}\)

When converting from base 10 to base 4, the result obtained was 142_(4). How can you tell an error was made?

Addition and Subtraction in Base Systems

Exercise \(\PageIndex{28}\)

Create the addition table for base 5.

Exercise \(\PageIndex{29}\)

How many addition rules are there for a base 7 system?

Exercise \(\PageIndex{30}\)

Calculate 34_(5) + 44_(5).

Exercise \(\PageIndex{31}\)

Calculate A7_(12) + 88_(12.)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{32}\)

Calculate 541_(6) − 233_(6.)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{33}\)

Calculate 5B_(12) − 1A_(12)_(.)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{34}\)

When adding in base 8, the result 911_(8) is found. How do we know a mistake was made?

Multiplication and Division in Base Systems

Exercise \(\PageIndex{35}\)

What is the process for creating the multiplication table for a base other than 10 ?

Exercise \(\PageIndex{36}\)

Create the multiplication table for base 7.

Exercise \(\PageIndex{37}\)

How many multiplication rules are there in a base 3 system?

Exercise \(\PageIndex{38}\)

Calculate \(14_7 \times 25_7\).

Exercise \(\PageIndex{39}\)

Calculate \(67_{12} \times 3 B_{12}\).

Exercise \(\PageIndex{40}\)

Calculate \(42_7 \div 5_7\).

Exercise \(\PageIndex{41}\)

Calculate \(38_{12} \div \mathrm{B}_{12}\).

Exercise \(\PageIndex{42}\)

When multiplying \(14_{12} \times 10_{12}\), the result 140 is found. How do we know a mistake was made?
